title: Carbon Emissions and Shareholder Value: Causal Evidence from the U.S. Power Utilities
Dirty Assets, Clean Opportunities: Private Equity Ownership of Fossil Fuels and the Energy Transition
abstract: Old, dirty assets often provide valuable opportunities for the development of new, clean technologies. I show that Private Equity (PE) firms are better able to realize these opportunities in the power sector. Using solar irradiance at fossil plants and investment tax credits, I find that PE firms are more likely to acquire fossil plants with exogenously greater solar opportunities. PE acquisitions lead to increased solar development nearby, even after accounting for selection effects. These results are driven by PE firms’ operational improvements and relationships with solar investors. My findings suggest that prohibiting PE fossil investments could unintentionally impede energy transition.
abstract_zh: 陈旧、高污染的资产往往为发展新型清洁技术提供了宝贵机会。本文表明，私募股权（PE）公司在电力行业中更能把握这些机会。利用化石电厂所在地的太阳能辐照度以及投资税收抵免政策，我发现，PE公司更倾向于收购那些外生地拥有更优太阳能条件的化石电厂。即使在考虑选择效应之后，PE收购仍会带动附近的太阳能开发增加。这些结果源于PE公司的运营改进及其与太阳能投资者之间的关系。我的研究发现表明，禁止PE投资化石燃料资产可能会无意中阻碍能源转型。
